'''Thomas Kuczynski''' (12 November 1944 – 19 August 2023) was a German [[statistician]] and economist.<ref name=TERMKlautwerwarwer>{{cite web|url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=1945|title=Kuczynski, Thomas * 12.11.1944 Wirtschaftshistoriker|author=Dieter Hoffmann|author-link=Dieter Hoffmann (historian)|work=„Wer war wer in der DDR?“|publisher=Ch. Links Verlag, Berlin & Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur, Berlin|accessdate=21 February 2016}}</ref>

For reasons of [[Nazi Germany|politics]] and [[Jewish question|race]] Kuczynski was born in [[Hendon|north-west]] [[London]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.freebmd.org.uk/cgi/information.pl?cite=rbICnItp2wDAfn7H8pVyQw&scan=1|title=Hendon birth registrations index: Kuczynski, Thomas E R M |accessdate=21 February 2016|work=FreeBMD|publisher=ONS}}</ref> Since 1947 he has lived in [[Berlin]], however.<ref name=TERMKlautwerwarwer/> Between 1988 and 1991 he served as the final director of the Institute for Economic History at the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|(East) German Academy of Sciences]]:<ref name=TERMKlautCD>{{cite web| url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/geld/thomas-kuczynski-karl-marx-ist-immer-anregend-1.364517|date=17 May 2010|title="Karl Marx ist immer anregend": DDR-Cheftheoretiker Thomas Kuczynski über die linke Antwort auf die Krise, wie er mit dem Dollar spekuliert hat und warum er sich keine Bücher leisten kann.|author1=Caspar Dohmen (as interviewer)|author2=Thomas Kuczynski (as interviewee) |publisher=Süddeutscher Verlag (Süddeutscher Zeitung), München|accessdate=21 February 2016}}</ref> the Institute had been established by [[Jürgen Kuczynski|his father]] in 1955.<ref name=JKlautwerwarwer>{{cite web|url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=1944|title=Kuczynski, Jürgen * 17.9.1904, † 6.8.1997 Wirtschaftshistoriker|author=Ilko-Sascha Kowalczuk|author-link=Ilko-Sascha Kowalczuk|work=„Wer war wer in der DDR?“|publisher=Ch. Links Verlag, Berlin & Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur, Berlin|accessdate=21 February 2016}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Thomas Kuczynski was a member of a prominent family of Berlin intellectuals. His grandfather, [[Robert René Kuczynski]], father, [[Jürgen Kuczynski]]<ref name=IndyobitJK>{{cite web | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-professor-jurgen-kuczynski-1245205.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-professor-jurgen-kuczynski-1245205.html |archive-date=2022-05-07 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title= Obituary: Professor Jurgen Kuczynski |author= David Childs |author-link= David Childs (academic) |work=[[The Independent]]|location=London| date=13 August 1997|accessdate=4 September 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and mother, [[Marguerite Kuczynski]] were all economists and/or statisticians. Thomas was born during the final year of the [[Second World War]], and in 1945 the defeat of [[Nazi Germany]] [[Aftermath of World War II|opened the way]] for the family to return, in 1947, to [[Berlin]], by now surrounded by the [[Soviet occupation zone]] in what remained of Germany. Kuczynski [[Abitur|successfully completed]] his secondary schooling at the Paul-Österreich Upper School in 1963.<ref name=TERMKlautwerwarwer/> Between 1963 and 1968 he attended the [[Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft Berlin|University of Applied Sciences for Engineering and Economics (''"Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft"'')]] at [[Karlshorst]] in what had become known in the west as [[East Berlin]]: here he studied [[Statistics]].<ref name=TERMKlautwerwarwer/> Thomas Kuczynski received his doctorate in 1972 for work on the closing period in Germany of the [[Great Depression]] which for these purposes he placed at 1932–33.<ref name=TERMKDiss>{{cite book|title=Das Ende der Weltwirtschaftskrise in Deutschland 1932/33|author=Thomas Kuczynski|date=1972|oclc=721632301}}</ref> His dissertation was supervised by [[Hans Mottek]].<ref name=TERMKlautwerwarwer/> 
{{Quote box
 | width =38%
 | align =right
 | quote = '''A "left of centre" economist on his relationship with money:'''<br>
:"You know, money is so necessary, like visiting the toilet. You cannot survive in this world without money. But I do not myself find it worthwhile to sit on the toilet permanently"
:''"Ach, wissen Sie, Geld ist so notwendig, wie aufs Klo zu gehen. Ohne Geld ist in dieser Welt nicht zu überleben. Aber ich persönlich sehe es nicht als eine erstrebenswerte Tätigkeit an, ständig auf dem Klo zu sitzen."''<ref name=TERMKlautCD/> {{right|''Thomas Kuczynski, 2010''}} }}
Between 1972 and 1991 Kuczynski worked as a research assistant / researcher at the Institute for [[Economic history]] at the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin]], serving as its last director during the run up to the [[Die Wende|political changes]] that led to the Academy's dissolution (and partial resurrection as the [[:de:Leibniz-Sozietät|Leibniz Society]]). Since [[German reunification|1991]] he has emerged as a freelance academic and writer.<ref name=TERMKlautwerwarwer/>
In recent years Thomas Kuczynski's public profile has been raised with the publication of his study of compensation claims for forced labour victims of the [[Nazi Germany|Nazi years]] (''"Entschädigungsansprüche für Zwangsarbeit im ‚Dritten Reich‘ auf der Basis der damals erzielten zusätzlichen Einnahmen und Gewinne"'').<ref name=EntschTERMK>{{cite journal| title=Entschädigungsansprüche für Zwangsarbeit im 'Dritten Reich' auf der Basis der damals erzielten zusätzlichen Einnahmen und Gewinne|author=Thomas Kuczynski|publisher=Stiftung fuer Sozialgeschichte des 20. Jahrhunderts, University of Bremen |url=https://www.zum.de/Faecher/Materialien/lehmann/files/imi/Kuczynski-Gutachten-Zwangsarbeit.pdf|accessdate=21 February 2016}}</ref> Kuczynski concluded that the German Federal Republic should pay victims of forced labour under Nazi Germany approximately 180 Billion Deutsche Marks. Later, in his book ''"Brosamen vom Herrentisch"'', he increased his estimate to 228 Billion Deutsche Marks (equivalent to €116 Billion).<ref name=Brosamen>{{cite book|title=Brosamen vom Herrentisch| author=Thomas Kuczynski|publisher=Verbrecher Verlag|date=31 August 2004|isbn=978-3-93584-337-9}}</ref>
In 2007 Kuczynski took part in the theatre project "Karl Marx: Das Kapital - Erster Band" (''"Karl Marx: Das Kapital - First volume"''), a show by [[Rimini Protokoll]] presenting a range of experts, mostly not normally to be found on a theatre stage, from various political and business backgrounds, giving their perspectives on [[Marxist philosophy|Marxian philosophy]] in general and on [[Capital: Critique of Political Economy|Das Kapital]] in particular.<ref name=Rimini>{{cite web|url=https://www.rimini-protokoll.de/website/en/project/karl-marx-das-kapital-erster-band|title=Karl Marx: Das Kapital - Erster Band|work=Rimini Protokoll (theatre group)|publisher=Rimini Protokoll Produktionsbüro, Berlin|accessdate=22 February 2016}} (English)</ref> Kuczynski claimed to eschew "-isms",<ref name=TERMKlautND04052013>{{cite web|url=http://www.neues-deutschland.de/artikel/820536.am-besten-marx-lektuere-verbieten.html|title="Am besten Marx-Lektüre verbieten" - Thomas Kuczynski hält nichts von -ismen und bevorzugt den Begriff des Marxschen Denkens|date=4 May 2013|publisher=Neues Deutschland Druckerei und Verlag GmbH, Berlin|accessdate=22 February 2016}}</ref> but it is hard to avoid concluding that much of his academic work is undertaken through an appropriately updated Marxist prism.<ref name=TERMKlautCD/> He was a member of the advisory council of the [[:de:Bildungsgemeinschaft SALZ|Bildungsgemeinschaft SALZ (''Soziales, Arbeit, Leben & Zukunft'')]], a left-of-centre think tank.

===Personal life and death===
Thomas Kuczynski was married to the writer-philosopher [[Rita Kuczynski]] between 1972 and 1998,<ref name=RKWallflower>{{cite book|title=Translator's foreword|work=Wall Flower: A Life on the German Border|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=R5GhCgAAQBAJ&q=%22Rita+Kuczynski%22+married&pg=PR18|author1=Rita Kuczynski|author2=Anthony J. Steinhoff (translator)|publisher=University of Toronto Press| date=2015| isbn=978-1-4426-4818-0}}</ref> though they separated in 1991.<ref name=RKwebpage>{{cite web|url=https://www.rita-kuczynski.de/wb8/pages/start/curriculum-vitae-de.php|title=Curriculum Vitae (de.)|publisher=Dr. Rita Kuczynski, Berlin|accessdate=22 February 2016}}</ref>

Kuczynski died on 19 August 2023, at the age of 78.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wirtschaftshistoriker Kuczynski gestorben |url=https://www.jungewelt.de/artikel/457832.pressemitteilung-wirtschaftshistoriker-kuczynski-gestorben.html |access-date=22 August 2023 |publisher=junge Welt |date=22 August 2023}}</ref>
